entry.title: MicroBooNE and the Panofsky Prize
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab reports that Sam Zeller was awarded the W.K.H. Panofsky Prize. The citation is for co-leadership of the MicroBooNE experiment, which advanced next-generation liquid-argon time projection chamber technology for neutrino detection.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab, CERN and SURF crews have started building the first of two cryostats, the insulated containers that will hold liquid argon for DUNE. Fermilab News also reports that physicists at the University of Texas at Arlington are working on the field cage and other detector components. Colorado State University marks the construction milestone as a founding member of DUNE.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CERN Courier reports that Francis Halzen was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. The IceCube site meanwhile continues its weekly reports from the South Pole station.

entry.title: KM3NeT/ARCA diffuse emission
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT published a search for all-sky and Galactic Ridge diffuse neutrino emission with early ARCA configurations of 6, 8, 19 and 21 detection units, with a total livetime of 640 days. The collaboration compares theoretical predictions with the ARCA data. The all-sky fit assumes a single power law.

entry.title: KM3NeT/ARCA stacking search
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT announced a stacking search for high-energy neutrino point sources with ARCA. It targets ultra-luminous infrared galaxies and blazars, and combines the signals from many astronomical objects of each class. The record gives no result.

entry.title: SBND cross sections
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SBND measured the total and single-differential inclusive electron-neutrino charged-current cross sections on argon. The sample is 95.2% electron neutrinos and 4.8% electron antineutrinos. The authors describe it as the highest-statistics inclusive measurement of this channel on argon to date and the first one using the Booster Neutrino Beam. They present the channel as an input to electron-neutrino appearance studies.

entry.title: JUNO ultrapure water
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. JUNO is a 20 kton liquid-scintillator detector designed primarily to determine the neutrino mass ordering. Because the scintillator is in direct contact with water during filling, the water must have a radium concentration below 50 μBq/m3. A paper from the collaboration describes a measurement system sensitive down to 3.9 μBq/m3 and an optimised 100 t/h production process that combines selective ion-exchange resin with membrane separation.

entry.title: Movable reactor near JUNO
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A phenomenology study considers a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within about 3 km of the JUNO detector. The authors state that no planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on θ13. They consider a microreactor of order 20 MWth, whose event rate in the large JUNO volume could probe the disappearance set by θ13.

entry.title: The paper proves that every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the ma
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves that every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is blind to a Majorana phase in open two-flavour oscillations. It also shows that a rate anisotropy in the unital case can act as an environmental phase reference. The result bears on any proposal to see a Majorana phase through decoherence in oscillation data.

entry.title: The authors give semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion i
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors give semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in neutrino ensembles in quasihomogeneous systems. They report agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of the mass ordering. Supernova simulations cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics directly, so such subgrid schemes matter for them.

entry.title: The paper studies whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande can constrain the primary cosmic-ra
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande can constrain the primary cosmic-ray spectrum through the atmospheric neutrino flux. The authors report that future detectors can distinguish cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, including uncertainties from neutrino cross sections and hadronic interactions. For atmospheric neutrino analyses, it turns the flux input into something the data themselves could test.

entry.title: The authors use low-energy solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain ano
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors use low-energy solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free U(1)_X dark photon models with kinetic and mass mixing. They derive limits for six benchmark models and find that their stringency is correlated with the leptonic charge assignments. It shows what dark matter detectors can say about new light mediators coupled to neutrinos.

entry.title: The paper constrains an ultralight vector boson of a gauged L_μ − L_τ symmetry through its effect on solar neu
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper constrains an ultralight vector boson of a gauged L_μ − L_τ symmetry through its effect on solar neutrino oscillations. Kinetic mixing with the photon produces a matter potential in the Sun that modifies Mikheyev–Smirnov–Wolfenstein conversion. The analysis uses solar measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande, and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The paper addresses the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which may contain Δ i
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper addresses the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which may contain Δ isobars alongside hyperons. The authors note that the contribution of this process to neutrino emissivity had not been explicitly determined before. The emissivity sets the cooling rate in neutron-star thermal evolution.
